title: Islanded NVLink partition investigation and mitigation notes
content:
Summary:

This note captures an investigation carried out in Nov–Dec 2025 into a reproducible performance regression we observed when GPUs in a single node became "islanded" (NVLink fabric partitioned due to firmware/hardware differences or BIOS settings). The symptom: sustained throughput drop (~30–45% tokens/s) and higher p95/p99 tail latency for production-like encoding+decoding workloads when model shards were mapped across the partition boundary.

Why we looked:
- Multiple customer incidents flagged elevated inference latency for large-context models on certain Dedicated nodes.
- We noticed these issues correlate with heterogeneous board revisions and mixed NVSwitch configurations in the same host rack.
- Existing serving runtime metrics pointed to longer all-reduce / KV cache sync intervals and more NCCL retries.

Hypothesis:
When the GPU interconnect graph becomes non-fully-connected (two or more NVLink islands), collective algorithms selected by NCCL (ring vs tree vs CollNet) and the kernel placement strategy interact poorly with our tensor-sharded execution and cause additional cross-island traffic to funnel through a smaller set of links (PCIe or limited NVLink bridges). This increases serialization and creates bursty cross-island microbursts, hurting sustained throughput and tail latency.

Testbed and constraints:
- Hardware: 8x A100-80GB per node mixtures (some nodes have NVSwitch v1, some v2); firmware: mixed (driver 535.54, CUDA 12.1).
- Software: serving-runtime revision bb7d3f (investigation branch islanded-nvlink), NCCL 2.18, PyTorch 2.2 (inference-only builds).
- Workloads: 1) synthetic allreduce microbenchmarks (nccl-tests) 2) production-like transformer decode pipeline (seq_len 2k, batch 1–8), 3) end-to-end token generation loop with KV cache reuse (long context reuse).
- Measurement: token/s throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, NCCL ops per second, PCIe util (nvidia-smi pcie), nvlink counters via nvidia-smi nvlink -c, kernel-level metrics via perf + CUPTI traces.

Methodology (quick):
1) Reproduce baseline on a fully-connected NVSwitch node. Record metrics.
2) Reproduce on a node intentionally partitioned (simulate by disabling NVLink ports or manipulating BIOS).
3) Run placement experiments: co-locate all shards inside one island vs spread across islands with same logical placement in serving runtime.
4) Instrument NCCL: enable NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0/1, NCCL_P2P_LEVEL, NCCL_IB_DISABLE to force fallback to PCIe.
5) Collect traces for slow paths and identify microburst windows.

Tests and key runs (representative):
- run A (baseline connected): nccl-allreduce 8x100MB: bandwidth 380 GB/s aggregate, avg latency 6.8 ms, tokens/s (model decode benchmark) = 1,420 t/s, p99 = 230 ms.
- run B (islanded, spread shards): nccl-allreduce 8x100MB: bandwidth 210 GB/s aggregate, avg latency 12.4 ms, tokens/s = 880 t/s, p99 = 410 ms.
- run C (islanded, islands-localized placement): nccl-allreduce inside-island 4x100MB x2 parallel: aggregate 360 GB/s, tokens/s = 1,300 t/s, p99 = 240 ms.

Primary observations: 
- Bandwidth loss is not uniform; cross-island allreduce shows reduced aggregate bandwidth and spikes in retry counts.
- NCCL chose ring-based algorithms for several collective ops that crossed the partition; ring across islands resulted in longer critical paths because hops had to traverse PCIe bridges with lower bisection than NVLink.
- KV cache sync phases created synchronized bursts of cross-island traffic (many small messages) that amplified PCIe latency and caused head-of-line blocking on the small number of cross-island links.
- Enabling CollNet in NCCL improved some patterns but increased memory pressure and latency variability for smaller message sizes.

Root cause breakdown (probable):
1) Topology mismatch: the runtime scheduler places tensor/pipeline shards without being topology-aware at fine granularity. When shards straddle islands, the communication pattern requires repeated cross-island exchanges.
2) Collective selection: NCCL's heuristics picked algorithms assuming high bisection bandwidth; when that assumption is false, the chosen algorithm performs poorly.
3) Microburst amplification: the interplay of synchronized inference stages (KV flush, attention-state sync) generates many small collectives at once which saturate constrained links.

Repro steps (short):
1) Boot node with mixed NVSwitch (or simulate by disabling NVLink ports).
2) Export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO; export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0; export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 to observe PCIe fallback.
3) Start serving-runtime branch with placement config that pins shards to alternating GPUs (0,4,1,5,...).
4) Run decode benchmark with seq_len 2k and batch 4, collect metrics.

Temporary mitigations we validated: 
- Topology-aware placement: prefer packing shard placements within an island (co-locate logically connected layers). This recovered ~90–95% of baseline throughput in tests.
- Staggered KV flush windows: add jitter across ranks to avoid synchronized small-message bursts. Reduced p99 by ~25% in the islanded case.
- NCCL tune knobs: forcing CollNet (NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=1) sometimes helps for large messages but worsened small-message latency. Setting NCCL_ALGO=ring or TREE explicitly gave predictable behavior; best is to select based on detected topology.
- Fallback policy: detect islanding at runtime (nvmlTopoGetGpuLinkInfo or nvidia-smi nvlink -g) and pin to conservative placement or prefer local-only collective implementations.

Longer-term mitigations and proposals: 
- Topology discovery + placement engine: implement a lightweight topology map at agent start and expose placement constraints in the shard planner. This should be integrated into the scheduler used by the serving runtime.
- Adaptive collective selection: add a small NCCL adapter layer that queries link bisection/bandwidth and toggles algorithm selection and chunking thresholds at job start. We can use NCCL tuning hints or wrap collectives.
- KV sync de-synchronization: change default KV sync to use randomized offsets or mellowed burst sizes when cross-island links are detected.
- Monitoring: add an "islanded" alert (SLO trigger) that watches per-link bandwidth imbalance and NCCL retry counts; link to automatic placement rollback to local packing.

Open questions and TODOs: 
- Should we always prefer island-local packing even if it increases tail latency for single-island hotspots? Need perf/SLAs discussion with product.
- How to best expose topology-aware constraints to customers of Dedicated vs Private deployments? Binary telemetry? Opt-in flags?
- Does CollNet licensing/compatibility vary across supported NCCL versions/cloud drivers? Need matrix.

Appendix A — Useful commands and snippets used during investigation:
- nvml topology: python snippet using pynvml to enumerate GPU link types (used to detect islands).
- nvlink counters: nvidia-smi nvlink -c 6 -g 0 to sample counter bucket.
- nccl-tests: mpirun -np 8 ./all_reduce_perf -b 1M -e 512M -f 2
- forced collnet: export NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=1; export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
- placement hack (serving-runtime flag): --shard-pack-policy=topology-aware (experimental)

Appendix B — Sample trace annotation (short):
- p99 spike frames mapped to time window [T+18ms..T+62ms]. CUPTI traces show repeated 8-16KiB send ops queued, with host blocking observed when PCIe TX queue saturated on the crossing bridges.

Appendix C — Quick benchmarks (numbers are averages over 10 runs):
- Fully connected node: 1420 +/- 45 t/s, p99 230ms, NCCL retries 0–2 per minute.
- Islanded, naive placement: 880 +/- 70 t/s, p99 410ms, NCCL retries 15–40 per minute.
- Islanded, topology-aware packing: 1,300 +/- 40 t/s, p99 245ms, NCCL retries 1–5 per minute.

References and links: 
- Slack discussion: #perf-investigations thread titled "islanded NVLink regressions" (see linked_artifacts)
- GitHub PR with placement prototype: /serving-runtime/pull/812
- JIRA ticket tracking customer incidents: JIRA-INF-1423

Concluding note: 
This investigation suggests the dominant wins come from topology-aware placement and small changes to KV-sync timing. CollNet and NCCL knob fiddling have situational benefit but are not a silver bullet. Next steps are to (1) land a conservative topology-aware placement option behind a flag, (2) add island-detection telemetry and alerts, and (3) run a limited Dedicated fleet pilot to validate at scale.
